categories.main_business_segments: Fuji Oil operates four main business segments: Vegetable Oils and Fats, Industrial Chocolate, Emulsified and Fermented Ingredients, and Soy-based Ingredients. These segments encompass the manufacturing and sale of processed edible oils, chocolate and cocoa products, emulsified and fermented food materials (such as creams and margarines), and a variety of soy protein products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced oil processing technologies, including enzymatic modification, crystallization control, and unique dispersion techniques (such as DTR technology). It also utilizes proprietary methods for producing cocoa butter equivalents (CBE), plant-based emulsification, fermentation for flavor and texture, and innovative soy protein extraction and processing (including USS method for soy milk). R&D focuses on combining these core technologies to create new plant-based food solutions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Fuji Oil primarily serves B2B customers in the food manufacturing industry, including confectionery, bakery, dairy, and processed food companies. Its products are used as intermediate ingredients by major food manufacturers, bakeries, patisseries, and food service providers globally.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally with significant presence in Japan, the Americas (notably the US and Brazil), Southeast Asia (Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia), China, and Europe (Belgium, Germany). Sales are well-diversified across these regions, with approximately 70% of employees based outside Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: Fuji Oil is positioned midstream in the food supply chain, acting as a key supplier of processed food ingredients to downstream food manufacturers and brands. It sources raw materials (such as palm oil, cocoa, and soybeans) and processes them into value-added ingredients for further use.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding high-value-added products, strengthening global supply chain resilience, and advancing sustainability (notably in palm oil and cocoa sourcing). R&D emphasizes plant-based innovation, health and nutrition, sustainable ingredient development, and upcycling of byproducts. The company is also investing in new technologies for alternative fats and proteins, and collaborating with external partners for open innovation.
categories.revenue_model: Fuji Oil generates revenue primarily through the sale of food ingredients and processed materials to B2B customers. Revenue is recognized upon delivery of goods, with some additional income from licensing, management fees, and dividends from subsidiaries.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include global and regional food ingredient manufacturers such as Cargill, Barry Callebaut, Wilmar, and J-Oil Mills. Fuji Oil differentiates itself through its technological expertise in plant-based ingredients and sustainability leadership, holding a strong position in the Asian market and a growing presence in the Americas and Europe.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2025, consolidated net sales reached 671.2 billion yen, with an operating profit of 9.9 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 2.2 billion yen. The company has experienced revenue growth (19% YoY), but profitability has been challenged by raw material price volatility, especially in cocoa. The group employs 5,654 people, with a significant global footprint.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Fuji Oil emphasizes the creation of sustainable, plant-based food ingredients that deliver both taste and health benefits. Its unique value lies in the fusion of proprietary technologies, ability to provide tailored solutions to customer challenges, and commitment to responsible sourcing and environmental stewardship. The company positions itself as a partner for innovation and sustainability in the global food industry.
